pages.text: Once you hit IV, you do not need to wait on a Research Station or HPCA to generate computation. Every IV datacenter component crafts from standard IV materials (Steel, Rubber, Copper, Stainless Steel, Platinum Wire, Fine Silver Wire, Silicon Wafers, and IV electronics) — $(bold)zero HPCA, zero Research Station, zero Data Bank prerequisites$().$(br2)The $(item)Air-Cooled Compute Rack$() needs no PCB coolant and outputs CWU/t straight over GT optical pipes.

pages.title: 3×5×2 Structure & Blade Scaling
pages.text: The 3×5 intake wall takes the controller in the centre and one $(item)Datacenter Hardware Hatch$() in an exposed intake casing. Load up to four IV blades through the hatch. Each adds 6 CWU/t. The second exhaust row takes energy, maintenance and an optional native computation transmitter for external optical links.

pages.title: Same-Tick Budget & Derating
pages.text: The rack implements GTCEu's `IOpticalComputationProvider` with a strict same-tick pool across all consumers:$(li)Simulation queries (`simulate=true`) never deduct CWU/t; only real consumption drains the 0–24 CWU/t budget.$(li)Pausing with a soft mallet, unfixed maintenance, 0 blades, or low power drops output to 0 CWU/t and logs the exact derate reason in the GUI.$(li)Cutting the optical pipe zeroes delivered CWU/t on the consumer side.

pages.title: Air Rack Heat Recovery
pages.text: Fit one fluid import and one fluid export hatch on the exhaust wall. Supply water or distilled water to recover steam while the rack provides computation.$(br2)Each mB of water yields up to 160 mB of steam. The IT-load cap keeps GT steam turbine recovery below 25% of the rack’s IT draw.
